findings.title: Recreate exit code moved from 4 to 3 and 4 reused
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, and 4 is now FEATURE_DISABLED. update-compatibility is invoked as a separate process, so callers branch on the numeric code, not this Java constant; recompiling in-repo Java does not update them. This PR does not change any operator production code that runs the check, and UpdateCommandDistTest never asserts an exit code: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks stderr text, and testWrongVersions only checks the incompatibility message. A caller still treating 4 as "incompatible, shut the cluster down first" will now take that path when the preview feature is merely off, and will not treat a real incompatibility (now exit 3) as recreate. That is the decision this tool exists to make; getting it backwards is either an unnecessary outage or a rolling update across incompatible versions. Lock both codes in the dist test and update every numeric comparison in the same change.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is documented as a failed rolling-upgrade decision
findings.body: The new exit-code row says exit 4 means "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" because rolling-updates is disabled. That is the same lead-in as exit 3, which means the deployment must be shut down before the new config is applied. The implementation does not evaluate compatibility in this case: UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata print "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." and return FEATURE_DISABLED before any metadata is read. The guide tells automation to rely on these codes. Describing 4 as a negative compatibility result will cause pipelines to recreate or drain the cluster when the only required action is to enable the feature and rerun the check.

findings.title: Default-strategy upgrade tests never enable rolling-updates
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, so spec.features.enabled is left unset for the null cases of testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount. Those cases still call deployKeycloak(..., true), which waits until the CR is ready, and then assert an upgrade status. The operator guide added in this PR says that while the feature is preview it must be enabled or the Operator will fail, including for the default <not set> strategy that mimics 26.1. As written, the default-strategy tests do not meet that precondition and will time out if the warning is true. If they pass, the warning is false and tells every operator user to turn on a preview feature or expect a failed reconcile. Enable the feature for every parameter value, and append it to any features already on the CR instead of setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) replacing the whole list, or narrow the caution if the default path is intentionally exempt.
